rules.statement: The compiled Official Context Package is the single canonical context for a Node: it applies to the Node itself and is the package meaning published to child Nodes.
rules.title: One official package
rules.why: A Node must not operate under one context while publishing a different truth to descendants.

rules.statement: Human context changes are authored in `CONTEXT.src.md`; generated context views, package contents, machine state, and harness adapters are not edited directly.
rules.title: Edit source, not generated output
rules.why: One editable source prevents drift between equivalent outputs.

rules.statement: Framework bookkeeping belongs under `.context/` and should not be required reading for normal human or agent work.
rules.title: Keep compiler bookkeeping out of the normal workflow
rules.why: IDs, snapshots, provenance, and digests are necessary for the compiler but should not dominate the user experience.

rules.statement: Context Sources are composed without implicit precedence; conflicts are resolved explicitly through local changes rather than Source order.
rules.title: No implicit Source precedence
rules.why: Hidden first-source-wins behavior would make composed context difficult to reason about and unsafe to maintain.

rules.statement: Every addressable context element has a stable ID independent of its title, wording, file location, and presentation.
rules.title: Stable identity
rules.why: Children must be able to remove, override, trace, or debug inherited elements even after human wording changes.

rules.statement: Published official contexts expose stable IDs for Rules and other elements that child Nodes may reference.
rules.title: Publish IDs that children may reference
rules.why: Users must be able to discover the correct target without searching hidden comments or machine YAML.

rules.statement: Keep the official entry context compact and use Topics to load deeper context only when needed; Topic targets distinguish Required from Optional material.
rules.title: Keep entry context small
rules.why: Context is scarce working memory and should be spent on information relevant to the current task.

rules.statement: `STATE.md` describes the current local project situation and is never inherited as governance by child Nodes.
rules.title: State stays local
rules.why: Temporary project reality is useful locally but is not a reusable Rule of descendants.

rules.statement: Project code and canonical project context must not depend on a particular LLM or agent harness; harness-specific files are thin generated adapters at the edge.
rules.title: Canonical context is model- and harness-neutral
rules.why: A project should remain portable across models and tools without duplicating its truth.

rules.statement: Keep `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` present when they are useful to the repository even when ContextCanon is present.
rules.title: Keep familiar repository documents useful
rules.why: ContextCanon should complement familiar project navigation rather than replace it.

rules.statement: Write technical documentation in precise, plain prose for intelligent readers; introduce unfamiliar concepts before using specialized terms and avoid unexplained internal shorthand, inflated marketing language, and unnecessary jargon.
rules.title: Write for intelligent readers
rules.why: Context should reduce interpretation effort for humans and models rather than create a private vocabulary barrier.

rules.statement: Before starting a new coherent development block, record a short purpose and checklist in the project's durable planning surface; use `PLAN.md` when the project follows this workflow convention.
rules.title: Plan a coherent change block before editing
rules.why: Repository state must explain what work is in progress even if the chat, model session, or tool run disappears.

rules.statement: When a listed step is actually complete, mark its `PLAN.md` checkbox `[x]` immediately rather than reconstructing completion at the end of a long session.
rules.title: Checkpoint completed plan items immediately
rules.why: Immediate checkpoints turn PLAN into a reliable recovery ledger instead of requiring plan archaeology after an interruption.

rules.statement: Put decisions, active constraints, accepted state, and next steps needed to resume work in repository documentation such as `PLAN.md`, `STATE.md`, or the project's equivalent rather than relying on chat history or model memory.
rules.title: Keep recovery-critical knowledge in the repository
rules.why: Long conversations and agent sessions are transient; the repository is the durable shared recovery point for humans and tools.

rules.statement: When the project owner resumes work after a short conversational interruption, explicitly says to continue, and reports no intervening repository changes, continue from the last established branch/PR state unless a repository operation gives evidence that it changed. Do not spend a new work cycle re-checking already established repository facts merely to prove that nothing happened.
rules.title: Resume recent explicit continuation without re-proving unchanged state
rules.why: In a controlled single-owner workflow, repeated defensive re-verification consumes the useful working window without adding evidence. Any stated or observed intervening change still invalidates this assumption.

rules.statement: For one coherent correction block, make the related authoring/code changes and run proportionate focused checks first; do not repeat the project's most expensive generated-output, integration, packaging, or full verification cycle after every micro-edit.
rules.title: Batch related edits before expensive final verification
rules.why: Final verification is valuable, but repeating it on superseded intermediate heads adds ceremony without increasing confidence in the candidate that will actually be reviewed or merged.

rules.statement: When the project owner explicitly approves a coherent implementation scope and says intermediate product review is unnecessary, mark the fast-run as active in the durable PLAN with its scope and exit condition, keep recovery checkpoints and focused verification inside bounded work blocks, and defer repeated PR-description polish, full CI, generated-output regeneration, and other review ceremony until the coherent review candidate. When the fast-run ends, record that closure before returning to ordinary review cadence.
rules.title: Use owner-approved fast-run blocks without weakening the final gate
rules.why: Explicit delegation can remove intermediate coordination cost without sacrificing recoverability. Visible start/scope/exit/closure boundaries prevent a long single-worker fast-run from becoming undocumented process state, while final human review and exact-head merge verification remain unchanged.

rules.statement: A coherent development block may be presented for project-owner review while understood and disclosed CI failures or generated drift remain. After explicit project-owner approval and before merging, require the exact current head to pass the project's complete merge-gate verification, including zero generated drift when generated canonical output is part of the project contract.
rules.title: Require exact-head green verification at the merge gate, not the first review gate
rules.why: Human review should happen before spending finalization effort on a candidate that may still change, while the accepted branch remains protected by a strict reproducibility gate.

rules.statement: Keep a review PR or equivalent change set open until the project owner explicitly approves the reviewed result.
rules.title: Do not merge without explicit project-owner approval
rules.why: Green automation proves only the properties it checks; it does not prove that the product, architecture, or documentation is acceptable to its human owner.

rules.statement: After a reviewed change is successfully merged into the accepted branch, reconcile the durable repository state that records the accepted baseline before starting the next coherent development block. Record the merge outcome in `PLAN.md`, update `STATE.md` or equivalent current-state documentation, and refresh README/CHANGELOG or review-status wording made stale by the merge when applicable.
rules.title: Close the post-merge baseline checkpoint before new development
rules.why: The merge itself creates project facts after the merge candidate was frozen. Without a post-merge checkpoint, the accepted code can be correct while recovery documentation still describes the pre-merge state.

rules.statement: Prefer deterministic mechanisms whenever behavior can be specified and computed exactly; use LLMs only for work that genuinely requires semantic interpretation.
rules.title: Deterministic skeleton, semantic intelligence on top
rules.why: Deterministic structure provides reproducibility and auditability, while LLM reasoning is most valuable where meaning rather than mechanics must be understood.

rules.statement: Keep the compiler pipeline explicit: `parser.py` parses authoring syntax into `model.py` structures; `compiler.py` resolves and composes semantics; `render.py` produces deterministic text; `outputs.py` compares or writes generated files; `cli.py` only orchestrates commands.
rules.title: Keep compiler stages separated
rules.why: Narrow one-way stages make compiler behavior easier to reason about, test, and debug without letting filesystem or presentation concerns leak into semantic truth.

rules.statement: A newly onboarded Context Node must receive human-owned stable identity; when ContextCanon generates that identity it creates a fresh UUID once and stores it in review state rather than deriving it from the Evidence digest.
rules.title: Keep new Node identity independent from Evidence identity
rules.why: Evidence identifies the exact bytes reviewed, while Node identity identifies one continuing project context; unrelated projects can contain identical evidence and must remain independent Nodes.

rules.statement: An onboarding proposal that reuses an existing Source must bind the Source Node ID, name, version, normalized digest, and package digest inspected by the semantic reviewer, and final acceptance must require that same immutable package.
rules.title: Bind reusable Sources to the exact reviewed package
rules.why: A different package version is a different review object even when the stable Source Node ID is unchanged; semantic review must not silently authorize content the reviewer never saw.

rules.statement: Before first onboarding publication, compile the proposed Node in staging, derive its actual compiler-owned output paths, and refuse publication when those outputs or canonical Context authoring/resource paths are already owned by the project.
rules.title: Do not seize project-owned paths during first adoption
rules.why: Adopting ContextCanon must never silently repurpose or overwrite an existing project file merely because its path collides with a generated ContextCanon output.

rules.statement: Treat first onboarding publication as one transaction-like state change; if publication fails before the acceptance record is complete, remove only the canonical/generated state and Source packages newly created by that failed attempt while preserving pre-existing accepted state.
rules.title: Make first-adoption publication rollback-safe
rules.why: An operator should be able to fix the failure and retry without first reconstructing whether the repository was left half-adopted.

rules.statement: Validate ContextCanon through concrete repository use cases before hardening abstractions into compiler code.
rules.title: Validate vertically before hardening
rules.why: Simple real workflows should shape the framework; implementation convenience must not force unnecessary ceremony on users.

rules.statement: Treat the repository documentation as the canonical design record once a decision is accepted; do not rely on reconstructing architecture from chat history.
rules.title: Repository documentation is the design record
rules.why: ContextCanon itself should demonstrate durable, reviewable project context.

rules.statement: Whenever ContextCanon generates a Markdown human gate that expects edits, mark every editable region with the same rendered `✏️ Editable ...` / `End editable ...` cues in addition to machine-only markers; HTML comments or heading wording must never be the only indication of editability.
rules.title: Mark human-editable generated Markdown with one visible convention
rules.why: Operators often review Markdown in preview mode where HTML comments disappear. One repeated visual grammar makes the workflow scannable and prevents each new review surface from inventing its own hidden interaction contract.

rules.statement: Use `uv` instead of direct `pip` installation when the required workflow is supported. For the current Windows development environment, prefer a dedicated PowerShell 7.x window and install a review branch or exact commit as a globally available uv tool with `uv tool install --force "git+https://github.com/SomeSunlight/context-canon.git@<ref>"`. Keep commands and implementation portable so Windows/PowerShell remains an operator environment, not a ContextCanon platform requirement; use another installer only when `uv` is unavailable or unsuitable for the concrete task.
rules.title: Prefer uv for ContextCanon development and tool installation
rules.why: A uv-managed tool install has proven more repeatable for the real ContextCanon operator workflow and avoids repeatedly reintroducing environment-specific `pip` setup across development sessions, while the framework itself must remain usable on other operating systems and shells.

rules.statement: A reusable Node in the ContextCanon Node Library composes Foundation only when its own semantics actually depend on Foundation. Standalone reusable Nodes remain independent, and consumers compose Foundation alongside them when both are wanted.
rules.title: Keep reusable Node dependencies explicit
rules.why: Reuse should not force unrelated transitive governance on consumers; explicit independent Sources are simpler than requiring consumers to remove a baseline that a reusable Node never needed.
